facts.statement: Parringtonia is known from a single fossil specimen discovered in the Anisian-age Manda Formation of Tanzania.
facts.quote: It is known from a single specimen, NHMUK R8646, found from the Anisian-age Manda Formation of Tanzania.

facts.statement: The known fossil material of Parringtonia is fragmentary, consisting of a maxilla and a few postcranial bones.
facts.quote: This specimen, like most archosaur material from the Manda Formation, is fragmentary, including only a maxilla and a few postcranial bones.

facts.statement: The specimen includes a right maxilla, left scapula, a partial ischium, nine vertebrae, and five osteoderms.
facts.quote: NHMUK R8646 consists of a right maxilla or upper jaw bone, a left scapula or shoulder blade, part of what might be the ischium bone of the pelvis, five complete and four partial dorsal vertebrae, three caudal vertebrae, and five osteoderms.

facts.statement: Evidence of unfused vertebrae indicates that the Parringtonia individual died while still immature.
facts.quote: Some vertebrae show suture lines where different parts have begun to fuse, indicating that the individual was immature when it died.

facts.statement: Parringtonia possesses five tooth sockets in its maxilla.
facts.quote: Parringtonia has five tooth sockets, Erpetosuchus granti only four, and Erpetosuchus sp. six or more.

facts.statement: Unlike related Erpetosuchus, the maxilla of Parringtonia features a foramen on its outer surface.
facts.quote: Unlike Erpetosuchus, Parringtonia has a foramen or hole on the outer surface of the maxilla.

facts.statement: The scapula of Parringtonia is distinguished by a small tubercle located over its shoulder socket.
facts.quote: The scapula of Parringtonia differs in that it has a small bump or tubercle over its shoulder socket.

facts.statement: Parringtonia is an extinct Triassic archosaur genus within the family Erpetosuchidae, represented by the type species Parringtonia gracilis.
facts.quote: Parringtonia is an extinct genus of Triassic archosaur within the family Erpetosuchidae, known from the type species Parringtonia gracilis.

facts.statement: Parringtonia was placed in the family Erpetosuchidae in 1970 and 1976 due to similarities in its scapula with Erpetosuchus.
facts.quote: In 1970 and 1976, Parringtonia was referred to the family Erpetosuchidae because of similarities between its scapula and that of the better known Erpetosuchus.

facts.statement: Nesbitt and Butler redescribed Parringtonia in 2012, including it in a phylogenetic analysis alongside Erpetosuchus.
facts.quote: Parringtonia was redescribed in 2012 by Nesbitt & Butler and included in a phylogenetic analysis along with Erpetosuchus.

facts.statement: Erpetosuchidae is defined by shared traits including teeth restricted to the front of the maxilla, a posterior maxilla thicker than tall, and lack of tooth serrations.
facts.quote: Three synapomorphies or shared characteristics were identified for Erpetosuchidae: teeth restricted to the anterior half of the maxilla, a posterior half of the maxilla that is thicker than it is tall, and no tooth serrations.

facts.statement: Recent analyses place Erpetosuchidae within the clade Suchia as the sister group to Aetosauria and Revueltosaurus, rather than as a sister group to Crocodylomorpha.
facts.quote: The removal of Gracilisuchus and Turfanosuchus from the analysis resulted in Erpetosuchidae nesting within the clade Suchia as the sister-taxon of Aetosauria plus Revueltosaurus clade, but not as a sister taxon of Crocodylomorpha as had previously been proposed.

facts.statement: Parringtonia lived during the Anisian age of the Triassic period.
facts.quote: It is known from a single specimen, NHMUK R8646, found from the Anisian-age Manda Formation of Tanzania.

facts.statement: Parringtonia shares similarities with Erpetosuchus, a related archosaur found in Scotland and the eastern United States.
facts.quote: They show similarities with those of another archosaur called Erpetosuchus, known from the Middle Triassic of Scotland and the eastern United States.

facts.statement: The phylogenetic placement of Parringtonia is debated, with some studies suggesting a relationship to Crocodylomorpha, though this is now questioned.
facts.quote: The phylogenetic placement of Parringtonia and Erpetosuchus are uncertain; some studies placed them close to the group Crocodylomorpha, which includes all modern crocodylians and many extinct forms that diversified after the Triassic, but this relationship has more recently been questioned.

facts.statement: Erpetosuchids possess an exceptionally large tuber on the scapula compared to other archosauriforms.
facts.quote: Unlike other archosauriforms that have a small tuber in the same location, the size of the tuber in erpetosuchids is exceptionally large in relation to the overall size of the scapula.

rejected.statement: Friedrich von Huene originally assigned Parringtonia to the group Pseudosuchia in 1939.
rejected.quote: When first described by Friedrich von Huene in 1939, Parringtonia was assigned to a group called Pseudosuchia.
rejected.reason: quote not found verbatim in the source

rejected.statement: A 2012 analysis confirmed that Parringtonia and Erpetosuchus are sister taxa forming the clade Erpetosuchidae.
rejected.quote: The analysis confirmed that Parringtonia and Erpetosuchus were sister taxa in their own clade, which was designated Erpetosuchidae.
